'''Jacobus Jan''' "'''Koos'''" '''Boomsma''' (born 1951) is a Dutch evolutionary biologist who studies [[evolution of eusociality|social evolution]] and the evolution of [[mating systems]].

== Education ==
Boomsma obtained an MSc and PhD degree in biology in 1976 and 1982 at the [[Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]].

== Career ==
Boomsma directs the Centre of Social Evolution and works as a professor of biology at the [[University of Copenhagen]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Biology |first=Department of |date=2008-06-25 |title=Staff |url=https://www1.bio.ku.dk/english/staff/?pure=en/persons/186303 |access-date=2022-07-05 |website=www1.bio.ku.dk |language=en}}</ref> He had done important work on ants of the genus ''[[Atta (ant)|Atta]]''. He is known most recently for the [[evolution of eusociality#Monogamy hypothesis|monogamy hypothesis]], which states that strict lifetime monogamy enabled the evolution of [[eusociality]] in the [[Hymenoptera]] (bees, ants, wasps, etc.).<ref name="boomsma07">Boomsma, J. (2007) Kin selection versus sexual selection: why the ends do not meet. Current Biology 17:R673-R683.</ref><ref name="boomsma09">Boomsma, J. (2009) Lifetime monogamy and the evolution of eusociality. Phil. Trans. of the Royal Society, B Series 364:3191-3208.</ref> He has also lent influential contributions to the fields of [[mutualisms]] and [[sexual conflict]] and heads research programmes in [[evolutionary medicine]], [[invasive species|invasive social syndromes]] and [[ant-fungus mutualism|fungal agriculture]]. He is a research associate at the [[Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute]] in Panama.
